newsitem.title: USA: Fla.bullet train seen 'financial disaster'- report.
newsitem.headline: Fla.bullet train seen 'financial disaster'- report.

text.p: Florida's proposed $5.3 billion high-speed rail system is "likely to be a financial disaster," a report by a Tallahassee think tank concluded.

"High speed rail is likely to cost more, carry fewer passengers and expose the state to greater financial risk than is presently anticipated," the James Madison Institute said in a report released Wednesday.

The report said Florida lacks the population density and connecting rail links that have made high-speed rail practical in Japan and Europe. It also said the proposed fares would be too high to compete with air and auto travel.

The 325-mile rail system would link Miami, Tampa and Orlando with electric trains travelling at up to 200 mph. A proposal allocating the first $30.5 million for the train system is currently before the state legislature.
Florida has pledged about $3 billion toward the project. The state is also seeking $300 million of federal funds over six years, plus a federal guarantee of the bonds that will finance it.

The institute said revenue projections for the project were "well beyond realistic" and were so fragile that even if they were met, "small operating and capital cost overruns could force a default on debt in less than 10 years."

The report said cost and usage projections for major transportation projects were notoriously over-optimistic, citing as examples the Denver International Airport, the English Channel Tunnel and Boston's Central Artery Tunnel.

"In the best case, this report estimates that the state of Florida would be required to increase its subsidy from $3 billion to $14 billion, and in the worst case to nearly $39 billion," the report said.
Florida Department of Transportation officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
Last year, the department awarded the project to the Florida Overland eXpress, or FOX, consortium.

The group is made up of Fluor Corp's Fluor Daniel Inc; Odebrecht Contractors of Florida, a unit of the Brazilian construction firm Odebrecht SA ; Bombardier Inc and GEC Alsthom Transport SA, the Paris-based company that developed France's famed Train A Grand Vitesse.
